note: 4,615 actual catalog-object locations from the pinned JPL SBDB orbital elements, propagated with a two-body approximation to 16 October 2026 TDB. Selection: asteroid records with semimajor axis 30–50 AU, perihelion at least 30 AU, and computed distance 30–50 AU. This is a selected, discovery-biased subset, not all Kuiper Belt objects or an unbiased density map. Point colors and sizes are display glyphs, not body sizes or measured colors. The faint Neptune ellipse is a JPL J2000 reference orbit; the Sun is physically scaled and subpixel. No synthetic filler points are added.
author: NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics; catalog visualization by Universe Scales
license: U.S. public-domain NASA media/data; credit the named science teams

operations: Retain actual JPL osculating elements and solve Kepler equation
Propagate mean anomaly to a common display epoch with a fixed two-body approximation
Select computed heliocentric distance 30–50 AU; retain true coordinates
Shuffle deterministically for runtime LOD; add no synthetic objects
